scenarios.user_message: I've got a flight next week and I'm honestly scared something will go wrong on it.
scenarios.rationale: Direct fear: anticipates a specific harm (flight), affect is dread. Inclusion 'anticipates harm/danger'.

scenarios.user_message: My daughter just started driving to school on her own. She's careful, but every time she pulls out of the drive I sit there braced for a phone call.
scenarios.rationale: Contextual fear: threat is a possible accident; the parent is braced/alarmed. Distinct from grief (no loss) and doubt.

scenarios.user_message: I can't stop worrying about the review meeting on Monday — it's honestly all I think about.
scenarios.rationale: Direct anxiety: ongoing, future-directed worry with rumination. Excl acute present threat.

scenarios.user_message: Work's fine, home's fine, nothing's actually wrong — but my head won't switch off lately and I keep running through everything that could go sideways.
scenarios.rationale: Ambiguous-but-resolvable: no concrete danger, but diffuse future-directed rumination = anxiety, not fear (no present threat) or confusion (clarity isn't lost).

scenarios.user_message: My coworker took credit for my project in front of the whole team today and I'm furious.
scenarios.rationale: Direct anger: hostile arousal triggered by a wrong, in the moment.

scenarios.user_message: I asked my landlord three times to fix the heating. Today he showed up, glanced at it, and left. I shut the door harder than I meant to.
scenarios.rationale: Contextual anger: heat/impulse in the moment triggered by obstruction; not settled aversion.

scenarios.user_message: I still can't get past how my brother treated me last year. I just resent him now.
scenarios.rationale: Direct resentment: persistent, cold ill-will that endures. Excl momentary anger.

scenarios.user_message: Every time my friend bails on plans last minute I say it's fine, but it's built up over months. I don't really feel like reaching out anymore.
scenarios.rationale: Contextual resentment: dislike endured over time, cold rather than hot.

scenarios.user_message: We're moving to a bigger place next month — good news — but I keep finding reasons to put off packing up the old flat. I've been here eight years.
scenarios.rationale: Contextual attachment: distress centres on letting go of a place held onto; identification with it.

scenarios.user_message: Everyone says sell my dad's old car — it just sits there costing insurance. I keep meaning to and then I leave it another month.
scenarios.rationale: Ambiguous-but-resolvable: could read as laziness, but the pull is not-letting-go of a kept object (attachment); secondary laziness present.

scenarios.user_message: My mum passed away in March and some days the sadness just flattens me.
scenarios.rationale: Direct grief: sorrow following a loss; low mournful affect.

scenarios.user_message: It's been six months since we had to put our dog down. I thought I'd be okay by now, but I still tear up when I see his leash by the door.
scenarios.rationale: Contextual grief: a loss has occurred; mourning persists. Distinct from separation-longing (the being is not merely absent).

scenarios.user_message: I really want that promotion. I think about it constantly — how it would feel to finally get it.
scenarios.rationale: Direct craving: pull toward something not yet possessed.

scenarios.user_message: I keep reopening the listing for a watch I can't really justify. I don't need it. I just really, really want it.
scenarios.rationale: Contextual craving: prospective object, wanting to obtain. Excl holding what one has (attachment).

scenarios.user_message: I got the raise I asked for and within a week I was already thinking it wasn't enough.
scenarios.rationale: Direct greed: never-enough quality; desire is insatiable.

scenarios.user_message: Business is better than I planned, but instead of easing off I keep chasing more accounts, more, more. My partner says I never call it enough.
scenarios.rationale: Contextual greed: excessive accumulation past need.

scenarios.user_message: I've read the setup instructions three times and I still don't understand what I'm meant to do.
scenarios.rationale: Direct confusion: clarity is lost about a task.

scenarios.user_message: Everyone's giving me advice about the reorg and none of it lines up. I can't tell what I think anymore, or which option is even the real choice.
scenarios.rationale: Ambiguous-but-resolvable: global loss of clarity (confusion) with a secondary either/or (doubt); primary is the fog, not a defined choice.

scenarios.user_message: I've got the job offer but now I'm genuinely unsure whether to take it or stay where I am.
scenarios.rationale: Direct doubt: hesitation between defined alternatives.

scenarios.user_message: On paper the move makes sense. My gut keeps saying wait. I go back and forth on it every hour.
scenarios.rationale: Ambiguous-but-resolvable: oscillation between two named options = doubt, not global confusion (the options are clear).

scenarios.user_message: I know I should apologise, but I really hate admitting I was the one who got it wrong.
scenarios.rationale: Direct pride: resistance rooted in self-elevation / not wanting to be seen as lesser.

scenarios.user_message: In the debrief I kept steering it back to what I'd handled well. Afterwards I realised I hadn't once acknowledged anyone else's part.
scenarios.rationale: Contextual pride: comparison/superiority emphasis.

scenarios.user_message: I completely blanked during the presentation and now I just want to hide.
scenarios.rationale: Direct shame: painful self-exposure with a shrinking/hiding impulse.

scenarios.user_message: I forgot my friend's birthday — genuinely forgot. When she mentioned it lightly I went hot in the face and changed the subject.
scenarios.rationale: Contextual shame: self-conscious exposure, wish to withdraw.

scenarios.user_message: My partner's away on a three-month posting. We talk every day, but the flat feels wrong without them and I keep counting the weeks.
scenarios.rationale: Contextual separation-longing: a specific loved one is absent (not lost); yearning for reunion.

scenarios.user_message: My best friend moved abroad in spring. We're still close, still text, but there's this ache I can't quite name when I pass the cafe we used to go to.
scenarios.rationale: Ambiguous-but-resolvable: reads near grief, but the friend is alive and merely absent -> separation-longing.

scenarios.user_message: My parents are getting older and I'm the only one nearby, so looking after them falls to me.
scenarios.rationale: Direct duty: a felt obligation tied to a role.

scenarios.user_message: Nobody else will run the fundraiser, so it's fallen to me again. It's mine to see through, even though I'm already stretched thin.
scenarios.rationale: Contextual duty (primary) with a secondary sense of burden; framed as 'mine to see through'.

scenarios.user_message: Between work, the kids, and my mother's appointments, it's all on me and it's just too much to carry.
scenarios.rationale: Direct burden (primary): responsibility experienced as weight/strain; secondary duty (the role) present.

scenarios.user_message: I said yes to chairing another group this week. I don't even remember agreeing. It just keeps piling on and I keep nodding.
scenarios.rationale: Ambiguous-but-resolvable: could read as duty, but the emphasis is heaviness/overload -> burden.

scenarios.user_message: I keep checking my bank balance even though nothing's changed. Money's just constantly on my mind.
scenarios.rationale: Direct money-concern: money/wealth is the explicit focus.

scenarios.user_message: We got through the month, but the car needs tyres and I've started shuffling which bill to pay late. I keep checking the account and turning it over at night.
scenarios.rationale: Contextual money-concern (primary) with secondary anxious rumination.

scenarios.user_message: After rent this month there's basically nothing left for groceries.
scenarios.rationale: Direct poverty: material lack/deprivation is the focus.

scenarios.user_message: The hours got cut at work and now I'm choosing between the electric bill and my kid's school trip. I lie awake scared we'll end up with nothing.
scenarios.rationale: Contextual poverty (primary lack/deprivation) with secondary fear of ending up with nothing.

scenarios.user_message: I've got a certification exam in two months and I've mapped out a study plan. Right now it's just head-down, grinding through the chapters each evening.
scenarios.rationale: Contextual diligence: active effort/industrious application.

scenarios.user_message: Some nights I really push at the side project; other nights I just open the file and stare. I want to stick with it, but I'm not sure what it's building toward.
scenarios.rationale: Ambiguous-but-resolvable: about effort/application (diligence, primary) with a secondary question of aim (purpose).

scenarios.user_message: The same three tasks have been on my list for a week and I just can't make myself start any of them.
scenarios.rationale: Direct laziness: disinclination to effort; can't get started.

scenarios.user_message: It's Sunday, the flat's a mess, I meant to meal-prep and do laundry, and instead I've been on the couch scrolling for four hours.
scenarios.rationale: Contextual laziness: avoidance of exertion / inertia.

scenarios.user_message: I've got a stable job but I keep asking what I'm actually working toward.
scenarios.rationale: Direct purpose: seeking a defined aim/direction.

scenarios.user_message: I ticked every box I set five years ago. Now I'm not sure what the next thing is even for, or which direction is mine to pick.
scenarios.rationale: Ambiguous-but-resolvable: reads near doubt, but the pull is toward a goal/direction -> purpose (primary), doubt secondary.

scenarios.user_message: I've really been wanting to understand how mortgages actually work before we buy.
scenarios.rationale: Direct curiosity: an active wish to know/understand.

scenarios.user_message: My kid asked me why the sky goes red at sunset and I realised I didn't actually know. Now I can't stop wanting to look it up.
scenarios.rationale: Contextual curiosity: a question is being pursued.

scenarios.user_message: After a year of practice I can finally read music fluently — it just clicks now.
scenarios.rationale: Direct knowledge: possession/grasp of an understanding.

scenarios.user_message: I used to nod along in budget meetings pretending I followed the numbers. This quarter I actually understand the whole model and it feels good.
scenarios.rationale: Contextual knowledge: framed as now understanding. Distinct from curiosity (already knowing).

scenarios.user_message: We're six months into trying to adopt and it's all waiting — forms, reviews, more waiting. I'm trying to hold steady but it's testing me.
scenarios.rationale: Contextual patience: forbearance/endurance under a drawn-out difficulty.

scenarios.user_message: My teenager barely speaks to me right now. I'm trying to ride it out like everyone says, but some days the constant coldness just gets under my skin.
scenarios.rationale: Ambiguous-but-resolvable: holding steady through difficulty (patience, primary) with secondary resentment building.

scenarios.user_message: Honestly, things are pretty good right now and I feel settled with where I am.
scenarios.rationale: Direct contentment: satisfaction / enough-ness.

scenarios.user_message: We didn't get the bigger house, and a year ago that would've stung. Now I look around our little place and it genuinely feels like enough.
scenarios.rationale: Contextual contentment: 'enough' quality; satisfied with what one has.

scenarios.user_message: After the deadline finally passed I took the weekend off-grid, and my mind feels quiet for the first time in weeks.
scenarios.rationale: Contextual calm: a quiet, undisturbed mind; absence of disturbance.

scenarios.user_message: I don't need anything fixed. I just want ten minutes somewhere my head isn't buzzing and racing through the week.
scenarios.rationale: Ambiguous-but-resolvable: a wish for a quiet/undisturbed mind (calm, primary) with secondary anxious racing.
